body: Ghana is actively pursuing investment and financing deals in Bangkok, Thailand, during the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG). The delegation, headed by Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Baah Forson and including Bank of Ghana Governor Dr. Johnson Pandit Asiama, is engaging with international investors and financial institutions.

The meetings, held from October 12 to 18, serve as a platform for Ghana to mobilize investment crucial for its "New Economy" agenda. This agenda, expected to be detailed in the 2027 Budget, aims to build on recent economic stabilization to foster sustained transformation through value addition, industrialization, and enhanced global competitiveness, with a focus on job creation.

Following a recent IMF staff-level engagement and Ghana's exit from the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) program, the Bangkok meetings are also a venue for advancing discussions on reforms under the new Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI). Dr. Forson is scheduled to meet with IMF leadership, senior World Bank officials, and other international finance representatives.

Dr. Asiama highlighted the importance of the meetings for bilateral engagements, allowing Ghana to directly present its economic program to potential investors and development partners. The Ministry of Finance team plans to intensify outreach in Thailand to attract investment into key economic sectors.

Globally, the meetings address challenges such as debt, energy security, and climate change, with discussions also touching on the impact of Artificial Intelligence and geopolitical conflicts on the economic outlook. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva has urged policymakers to take necessary actions, while World Bank Group President Ajay Banga noted the resilience of the global economy but pointed to pressures on developing countries.

body: Ghana’s ultimate economic salvation lies not in shifting geopolitical allegiances, but in a radical domestic structural transformation, Dr Richmond Akwasi Atuahene, a Financial Analyst, has asserted.
“Joining a new economic bloc will not cure the systemic vulnerabilities of the Ghanaian economy,” he explained, in an exclusive interview with Ghana News Agency (GNA).

The Cabinet of Ghana is taking steps toward a BRICS application, reflecting a desire to escape Western-dominated institutional conditionalities. The BRICS is an international organisation currently comprising ten countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates.

The Foreign Minister, Samuel Okudzeto-Ablakwa, recently, during a joint press briefing with Indian External Affairs Minister, Dr Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, announced a Cabinet decision for Ghana to formally apply for membership of BRICS, which had generated discussions across academia, economists, civil society organisations and the public.

Re-orienting Ghana’s economic destiny must be the topmost priority, Dr Atuahene, argues, rather than relying on external bodies – whether the IMF or BRICS. Ghana must dismantle the colonial-era, affectionately primed “Guggisberg economy” and replace it with a modern, self-sustaining, value-added model, the analyst said.

The term “Guggisberg Economy”—coined from the legacy of colonial Governor Gordon Guggisberg—defines an economic structure optimized strictly to extract and export raw materials, while relying heavily on imported finished goods.

body: Ghanaian officials are actively engaging with investors in Bangkok, Thailand, during the IMF-World Bank meetings to reassure them about the nation's economic outlook and reform commitments. This outreach follows the successful conclusion of the country's US$3 billion International Monetary Fund (IMF) bailout program.

The meetings, held from October 12-18, mark Ghana's first participation since transitioning from the IMF's Extended Credit Facility (ECF) to a non-financing Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI). This new arrangement prioritizes policy monitoring and reform implementation over direct financial aid.

Representatives from the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Ghana are scheduled to meet with investor groups to detail economic conditions, outline the government's policy direction, and explore avenues for future collaboration. These discussions aim to solidify the progress achieved during the IMF-supported program.

Sustaining these economic gains will hinge on maintaining fiscal discipline, effective debt management, enhancing revenue collection, and continuing reform efforts beyond the bailout period. Under the PCI, Ghana will not receive new funding from the IMF, underscoring the need for a credible economic policy framework and sound financial management to ensure macroeconomic stability.

The meetings in Bangkok provide Ghana with a platform to articulate its strategy for preserving economic stability, managing public debt, and continuing reforms without reliance on further IMF disbursements. Investors are expected to scrutinize the government's commitments alongside tangible progress on fiscal targets, expenditure control, and debt sustainability.

articles.lead: The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) has initiated an investment drive across Northern Ghana, focusing on actively mobilizing capital rather than solely attracting it. The delegation will also visit operational businesses to assess investments and identify expansion opportunities. GIPA's Chief Executive Officer, Simon Madjie, stated that Northern Ghana possesses significant potential for commercial agriculture, agro-processing, livestock, renewable energy, tourism, manufacturing, mining, logistics, and cross-border trade, which can foster industrialization and improve livelihoods. The roadshow seeks to convert identified opportunities into enterprises, partnerships, and jobs, promoting balanced economic growth across Ghana.

body: International affairs analyst Prince Anuwar-Sadat Amadu has advised the Ghanaian government to ensure that the nation's bid to join BRICS is guided by national interests, thorough economic analysis, and strategic diplomatic considerations. While acknowledging potential economic and diplomatic benefits, Amadu cautioned against viewing BRICS membership as an automatic solution to Ghana's economic challenges.

Amadu emphasized that the decision to join BRICS should be assessed within the context of the evolving global order, Ghana's constitutional obligations, its established foreign policy traditions, and the practical advantages the country could gain. He noted that BRICS reflects the growing influence of emerging economies in a global system historically dominated by Western powers.

The analyst highlighted that the central question for Ghana should be whether BRICS membership will advance its economic transformation and diplomatic interests. Potential benefits could include trade diversification, foreign direct investment, industrial development, technology transfer, and infrastructure financing. However, he stressed that membership alone does not guarantee financial assistance or economic growth.

Amadu also pointed out that Ghana's strategy should focus on strengthening domestic industrialization and value addition, rather than solely diversifying trading partners. He suggested that Ghana could derive greater benefits from its natural resources through local processing and industrial development, measuring the success of BRICS engagement by its contribution to producing and exporting more value-added goods.

Diplomatically, Amadu advised Ghana to consider how BRICS membership might affect its relationships with existing development partners. He advocated for a strategy of strategic autonomy and multi-alignment, allowing Ghana to deepen ties with BRICS members without compromising cooperation with Western partners and international financial institutions.

Furthermore, Amadu called for transparency regarding the obligations Ghana might assume, including financial commitments and institutional arrangements. He stressed the importance of parliamentary oversight and public accountability in the national discussion surrounding this significant foreign policy decision.

Dr Jinapor said the government had continued investing in transmission infrastructure, with several projects ongoing across the country. He cited the commencement of the process towards constructing the Ho–Asiekpe transmission line as part of efforts to strengthen the national grid.

articles.dek: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh – Minister of Health. Ghana has confirmed three cases of yellow fever in the Upper West Region, with all three resulting in deaths, the Minister of Health, Mr Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has announced.

articles.takeaway: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh – Minister of Health.
body: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh – Minister of Health. Ghana has confirmed three cases of yellow fever in the Upper West Region, with all three resulting in deaths, the Minister of Health, Mr Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has announced.
The confirmation follows laboratory tests conducted on samples from suspected cases at the Institut Pasteur, a World Health Organisation (WHO)-accredited laboratory in Dakar, Senegal.

The Minister, addressing a press conference in Accra on Friday, said the cases were confirmed out of 450 suspected cases. He said the Ghana Health Service (GHS) would begin a mass vaccination campaign in the affected region next week to contain the outbreak.

The campaign would target people aged nine months to 60 years. Mr Akandoh advised that yellow fever was not transmitted through direct person-to-person contact and urged the public to remain calm while observing the necessary preventive measures.
The Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the GHS and the WHO, has declared an outbreak in the affected districts of the Upper West Region following the laboratory confirmation.
The response includes measures to contain the outbreak and protect communities at risk. The WHO describes yellow fever as an acute viral disease transmitted through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

body: Ghana has hosted a South-South Regional REDD+ Study Visit and Knowledge Exchange Workshop, to accelerate readiness among West African countries to access results-based climate finance for reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation.

The workshop brought together representatives from Benin, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone to share experiences, strengthen forest governance and identify practical pathways towards accessing climate finance.

Mr Timothy Ataboadey Awotiirim, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Forestry Commission, said REDD+ readiness constituted the first phase of the Warsaw Framework and provided the foundation for countries to access results-based payments.
He said participating countries were developing key systems, including national forest monitoring, forest reference emission levels, safeguards information systems and national REDD+ strategies.

Mr Awotiirim said Ghana had made significant progress in establishing those systems, including submitting its forest reference emission level to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), for technical assessment and strengthening forest monitoring and carbon accounting arrangements.
Ghana had also integrated REDD+ into its Biennial Transparency Report through the Ghana Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme, he said. “Those systems have now been tested where it counts.

body: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has issued a warning to the public regarding 20 mobile loan applications that are operating without the necessary approval from the central bank. These digital lenders are providing credit services in violation of the Directive for Digital Credit Service Providers in Ghana.

The Bank stated that the operations of these unlicensed providers pose significant risks to users, particularly concerning customer data privacy, consumer protection, and adherence to financial sector regulations. The BoG has identified the following applications as operating without authorization: Agile Loan, AmanaPay, CashWay, Foutou Credit, HastyCredit, InsCash, KudiNow, LendAura, Lever Credit, LoanGlide, NovaCedi, Palm Loan, PocketLoan, Rite Credit, SikaCare, SikaNow, Susu Loan, Taploan Up, Temivo Cedi, and Zatuloan.

To safeguard consumers and maintain the integrity of the financial sector, the Bank of Ghana strongly advises the public to exclusively engage with financial institutions and digital credit providers that have been duly licensed and approved by the central bank.

The Bank of Ghana is actively collaborating with relevant state agencies to identify, investigate, and take appropriate enforcement actions against these unauthorized operators. These efforts are crucial for protecting consumers and ensuring the overall safety, integrity, and stability of Ghana's financial system.

body: Edmond Kombat has been named the Energy Sector Reform Programme (ESRP) Champion of the Year 2026 for his work in the petroleum sector. The award acknowledges his role in advancing reforms within Ghana's energy sector.

The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr. John Abdulai Jinapor, presented the award during the Energy Sector Performance Review Retreat. This recognition highlights Kombat's significant contributions to the objectives of the Energy Sector Recovery Programme.

The ESRP Champion Award, established in 2025, specifically honors leaders of institutions within the energy sector. It focuses on individuals who have demonstrably advanced the goals of the Energy Sector Recovery Programme.

Key areas of achievement considered for the award include improvements in revenue generation, cost reduction, operational efficiency, and good governance. These factors are crucial for enhancing the financial stability and overall performance of Ghana's energy sector.
